newsitem.title: UK: U.S. banks threaten life insurance agents -report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. banks threaten life insurance agents -report.

text.p: Banks will increase their share of the U.S. individual annuity market significantly over the next four years at the expense of life insurance agents, a report said on Friday.

"Although hampered by restrictive legislation, banks have won a number of major legal victories in recent years," management consultant Datamonitor said in its report "The future of the US insurance agent 1996-2000".
"It is likely that 1997 will see more liberalisation in this area, allowing banks to compete even more effectively for this kind of business," it added.

Banks will increase their market share of individual annuity business to 40.8 percent by 2000 from 24.4 percent in 1995, the report said, noting that agency sales forces tend to be much more costly than other distribution channels.

To keep costs down, insurers will have to improve staff retention and improve market conduct, the report said. "Scandals cost money, both in terms of lost sales, fines and the time spent in dealing with the aftermath."
